title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 119
paragraphs: When the Scythians made this proposal, the kings who had come from the various nations took counsel together, and their opinions were divided. The kings of the Gelonians, Budinoi, and Sauromatai agreed among themselves and accepted the proposal that they should help the Scythians. But those of the Agathyrsians, Neuroi, Androphagoi, Melanchlainoi, and Tauroi answered the Scythians as follows: “If you had not been the first to wrong the Persians and begin the war, we should have thought you spoke justly in asking for what you now ask, and we should have yielded to your request and shared your fortunes. As it is, however, you invaded their land without us, and ruled the Persians for as long as God permitted; and now they in turn, since the same God stirs them up, are repaying you in kind. As for us, neither at that time did we do those men any wrong, nor shall we now attempt to wrong them unprovoked. If, however, the Persians come against our land too, and wrong us first, we too will refuse to submit; but until we see that, we shall remain by ourselves. For we hold the opinion that the Persians have come not against us, but against those who were the authors of the wrong.”
